digest.component_or_area: graph link store and inbound reconciler
propositions: Link writes are relation-scoped via (target_id, relation) keying, allowing one ordered pair to hold multiple relations (e.g., blocks and relates_to) simultaneously, but removal is pair-scoped with no relation parameter, causing asymmetry.

When a pair holds two relations and a peer deletion record names one relation, the outbound differ may emit no link mutation due to direction-agnostic vendor-type deduplication, causing the inbound removal record to reach guard G5 and decline permanently, preventing reconciliation convergence.

Guard G5 in _inbound_unlink_one declines to unlink when the pair's most-recent net-active relation differs from the vanished peer relation, and the decline re-emits every pass, resulting in non-convergence visible only as log lines.

The fix adds relation-scoped removal at the graph layer (remove_dependency, symmetric with add_dependency) and threads an optional relation parameter through the unlink CLI and library facade while maintaining backward compatibility for pair-scoped behavior when no relation is specified.

For a double-related pair where a peer deletes one relation, relation-scoped removal of the exactly-mirrored relation allows convergence while preserving the safety invariant that no link the peer still carries is ever removed.
